words.desc: The Christian season of preparation covering the four Sundays before December 25.
The date that marks a whole number of years since a meaningful event, especially a marriage.
The first day of the fourth month, when people play harmless tricks and hoaxes.
A national holiday on January 26 marking the arrival of the First Fleet at Sydney Cove.
A spring harvest festival in Punjab that also marks the founding of the Khalsa in Sikhism.
France's national holiday on July 14, marking the storming of a Paris fortress in 1789.
A Hindu festival in autumn where sisters honour brothers and pray for their long life.
A set of three Assamese festivals tied to the farming calendar, the biggest being the spring new year.
The date each year that marks when a person was born.
A late-November shopping event in which retailers offer huge discounts on many products.
A British celebration every November 5 with fireworks, recalling a failed plot to blow up Parliament.
A public holiday on December 26 in Britain and many Commonwealth countries.
A Buddhist holy day on the full moon of May, marking the founder's birth and enlightenment.
A national holiday on July 1 celebrating the country's confederation in 1867.
A festive season of street celebrations with music, costumes and dancing before Lent begins.
A Christian holiday on December 25 marking the birth of Jesus, also widely celebrated with gifts.
The evening before December 25, when many families hang stockings and await gifts.
An evergreen, real or artificial, decorated with lights and ornaments during the December holidays.
Small pieces of coloured paper thrown in the air during celebrations such as weddings.
A major Hindu festival of lights celebrating the victory of light over darkness each autumn.
A major Bengali festival honouring a warrior goddess with elaborate temporary shrines and sculpted images.
A Hindu festival celebrating the triumph of good over evil, marked by burning giant effigies.
An annual event on April 22 promoting environmental protection around the world.
A Christian spring festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus.
A major Muslim festival, celebrated twice a year with prayers, feasts and gifts.
A Christian feast on January 6 celebrating the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus.
An annual occasion dedicated to honouring dads and other paternal figures.
A festive public celebration in Spanish-speaking countries, often honouring a patron saint.
Explosive devices that burst into colourful light and loud bangs in the sky for celebrations.
A Hindu festival celebrating the birth of the elephant-headed god of new beginnings.
The solemn Christian day commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus, observed two days before the resurrection feast.
An event at which students formally receive recognition for completing a course of study.
The Marathi new year, celebrated in spring by raising a decorated pole outside homes.
A Sikh festival marking the birth anniversary of a Guru, especially Guru Nanak.
A celebration on October 31 when people wear disguises and children collect sweets door to door.
The Japanese tradition of enjoying the beauty of blooming cherry blossoms, often with picnics.
An eight-day Jewish festival of lights recalling the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem.
A celebration giving thanks for the gathering of crops at the end of the growing season.
A Hindu spring festival where people joyfully throw coloured powder and water at each other.
A national holiday celebrating the anniversary of a country becoming free from foreign rule.
A Hindu festival marking the birth of Krishna, celebrated with midnight prayers and fasting.
A US federal holiday on June 19 commemorating the end of slavery in Texas in 1865.
A Hindu day when married women fast from sunrise to moonrise for their husbands' wellbeing.
A week-long African American cultural celebration of heritage held from December 26 to January 1.
A public holiday honouring workers and their achievements, held in early September in America.
The celebration on the fifteenth night of the Chinese lunar new year, lit by glowing paper lights.
A forty-day Christian season of fasting and reflection leading up to the spring resurrection feast.
A Punjabi winter festival celebrated around a bonfire to mark the end of the coldest season.
A Thai festival where people float small decorated baskets on rivers under the full moon.
A Hindu festival honouring Lord Shiva, observed with an all-night vigil, fasting and prayers.
A Hindu festival in mid-January marking the solar transition into Capricorn, famous for kite flying.
The Tuesday before Lent, celebrated with parades and parties, especially in New Orleans.
A US public holiday in late May honouring military personnel who died in service.
An East Asian harvest celebration held on the full moon of the eighth lunar month.
A celebration held around the year's longest stretch of daylight, popular in Scandinavia.
A yearly occasion for honouring mums and the role they play in family life.
A Hindu festival of nine nights honouring the divine feminine with fasting, worship and dance.
The celebration held as one calendar cycle ends and the next begins at midnight.
A Japanese Buddhist summer custom honouring the spirits of ancestors who return home.
A famous annual folk festival in Munich with giant tents, brass bands and Bavarian food.
A Kerala harvest festival celebrating a legendary king's return with feasts and floral designs.
A Jewish spring festival commemorating the Israelites' liberation from slavery in ancient Egypt.
A Tamil harvest festival in mid-January, named after a dish of rice boiled in milk.
A Hindu festival honouring the bond between siblings, marked by tying a sacred thread.
The ninth month of the Islamic calendar, when Muslims fast from dawn until sunset.
A national holiday celebrating the date a country's constitution came into effect.
The Jewish New Year, a two-day holiday that begins the High Holy Days in autumn.
The March 17 feast honouring Ireland's patron, celebrated worldwide with green clothing and parades.
An ancient Gaelic festival marking the end of harvest and the start of winter.
Either of the two yearly moments when the sun appears farthest north or south of the equator.
The traditional Thai New Year in April, famous for its joyful nationwide water fights.
The Chinese Lunar New Year, the most important holiday in the Chinese calendar.
A Hindu monsoon festival in which women celebrate marital devotion with swings, songs and fasting.
The Vietnamese Lunar New Year, the country's most important holiday for family reunions.
A North American autumn holiday when families share a large meal to express gratitude.
The new year festival of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, celebrated in spring.
An annual holiday on February 14 when people celebrate love with cards, flowers and gifts.
The Kerala new year in mid-April, when families wake to view an auspicious arrangement first thing.
A ceremony in which two people are married, often followed by a celebration.
The holiest day of the Jewish year, observed with a full day of fasting and prayer.
